sections.label: Licensed moneylending Bill amendments
sections.summary: The Bill proposes amendments from engagements as part of MinLaw's efforts to enhance the licensed moneylending industry, seeking three main things.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Today’s Bill proposes amendments that arose from these engagements and are part of the Ministry of Law's (MinLaw) ongoing efforts to enhance the licensed moneylending industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to do three main things: first, improve data sharing and usage policies; second, enhance MLCB’s functions through the sharing and use of data maintained by the MLCB; and third, facilitate digitalisation in the licensed moneylending industry.

sections.label: Clause 26 data sharing
sections.summary: Clause 26 introduces new provisions to align the licensed moneylending data sharing framework with the whole-of-Government data sharing approach.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 26 of the Bill introduces new provisions to align the licensed moneylending data sharing framework with the whole-of-Government data sharing approach.

sections.label: Clause 16 borrower information disclosure
sections.summary: Clause 16 introduces amendments to allow licensed moneylenders to disclose borrower information to more third parties, such as a prescribed list of credit bureaux.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This may enable over-borrowing by individuals who choose to withhold or inaccurately declare their credit information.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Hence, clause 16 introduces amendments to allow licensed moneylenders to disclose borrower information to more third parties, such as a prescribed list of credit bureaux.

sections.label: Comprehensive credit checks for moneylenders
sections.summary: With this amendment, licensed moneylenders will be able to conduct more comprehensive credit checks before granting a loan, helping them manage credit risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: With this amendment, licensed moneylenders will be able to conduct more comprehensive credit checks before granting a loan, thereby helping them manage their credit risk.

sections.label: Clause 8 statements of account
sections.summary: Clause 8 allows licensed moneylenders to provide borrowers with statements of account through modes of communication other than mail and email.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 8 of the Bill allows licensed moneylenders to provide borrowers with statements of account through modes of communication other than mail and email.

sections.label: Clause 7 interest rate advertising
sections.summary: Clause 7 mandates that the rate of interest charged stated in any advertising or marketing material be stated as a percentage per annum, month or other period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To prevent miscommunication between the borrower and the licensed moneylender, clause 7 mandates that the rate of interest charged stated in any advertising or marketing material, be stated as a percentage per annum, month or other period that the licensed moneylender charges for offering loans.

sections.label: Surety credit report consent
sections.summary: The amendment would let licensed moneylenders request a surety's credit report without the surety's consent, though some sureties may not know this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I have some concerns about the proposed amendment to permit a licensed moneylender to request from the credit bureau a credit report on a surety without having to obtain the surety's consent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While I am generally supportive of this measure, there may be instances where persons who have agreed to become sureties are not aware that their credit reports can be accessed by licensed moneylenders.

sections.label: Moneylender AML/CFT measures
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would share the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism measures for this sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry also share about the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) measures for this sector?

sections.label: Credit reporting process changes
sections.summary: The Bill changes the credit reporting process, allowing moneylenders to request credit reports on sureties without explicit consent, potentially streamlining loan approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Borrowing could potentially be made easier as the Bill will bring changes to the credit reporting process, which will allow moneylenders to request credit reports on sureties without explicit consent, potentially streamlining the loan approval process.

sections.label: Credit bureau privacy concerns
sections.summary: The passage asks whether expanded credit bureau authority and data sharing with public sector agencies raise privacy concerns and deter borrowing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will this expanded authority of the designated credit bureaus and data sharing with public sector agencies raise privacy concerns among borrowers and potentially deter borrowing?

sections.label: Wrongful payment demands offence
sections.summary: The amendment introduces a new criminal offence for wrongful demands of payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the amendment, there is also the introduction of a new criminal offence for wrongful demands of payment.

sections.label: Prescribing social service agencies
sections.summary: The passage states the intention to prescribe social service agencies that have been helping borrowers negotiate debt consolidation loans or restructuring plans with licensed moneylenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For a start, we intend to prescribe social service agencies (SSAs) which have been assisting borrowers in negotiating debt consolidation loans or restructuring plans with licensed moneylenders.

sections.label: Penalties for licensee offence
sections.summary: Licensees who commit this offence can be fined up to $20,000 or imprisoned up to six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Licensees found to have committed this offence can be fined up to $20,000 or imprisoned up to six months, or both.

sections.label: Proposed amendments to moneylending Act
sections.summary: The proposed amendments will allow data use aligned with whole-of-Government standards and facilitate better business practices by licensed moneylenders, while MinLaw monitors standards and protects borrowers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the Act will allow data to be used in meaningful ways that are aligned with the whole-of-Government standards and will facilitate better business practices by licensed moneylenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: MinLaw will continue to monitor and improve the standards of the licensed moneylending industry while ensuring that borrowers are adequately protected.
